name: Exact Corner Criterion for an Ample Two-Row Assembly
statement: In an ample two-row assembly $V=(B_0,D_0,D_1,B_1)$ with $C=B_0\cup B_1=D_0\cap D_1$, define $T_x$ as the intersection of the old sections containing $x$. Its corners are exactly: constant-row vertices $(x,b,b)$ where $(x,b)$ is a corner of $H=(B_0,B_1)$ incident with the layer coordinate; and nonconstant-row vertices $(x,1-b,b)$ where $(x,b)$ is a corner of $K=(D_1,D_0)$ and either $x\notin C$ or the old projection of its corner cube lies in $T_x$. Thus $V$ is cornerless exactly when the first set is empty and every corner of $K$ lies over $C$ but fails this cube-containment test.
proof: A constant-row word has both new-coordinate neighbours, so its full incident cube exists precisely when its old section corner cube also lies in the opposite section, which is the stated incident corner of $H$. A nonconstant-row word outside $C$ has no new-coordinate neighbours, making its corner condition identical to that in $K$. Over $C$, the new neighbours occur in each old section containing the word, and the full incident cube exists precisely when the projected $K$ corner cube lies in their intersection $T_x$.
comments: This is a first-corner criterion; it does not claim that every permitted corner extends to an acyclic unique-sink orientation.
